text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.

- Authorities are not prepared enough for taking care of the growing number of elderly people, Tor Inge Romoeren, head of the Norwegian Research Council, says. The government plans to spend an additional 30 billion crowns on the elderly by 2001, but still no one knows how they spend the 26 billion crowns already granted to care of elderly, Romoeren says.
- Norway's second largest commercial bank Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse and the country's largest insurer Storebrand signed a final merger plan on Tuesday.

- Environmental action group Greenpeace believes the American Monarch shipping vessel owned by Norway Seafoods, the world's largest catcher and processor of white fish, will be granted a licence to fish in Chile. Greenpeace says it will appeal to the Supreme Court if the licence goes through.

- Den norske Bank (DnB) has raised its bid for mortgage lender BNbank by five crowns to 203.50 crowns per share. DnB says it will apply for a concession to takeover BNbank regardless of the level of acceptance from BNbank shareholders.

- Norwegian and foreign brokers will earn millions from Norway's state Petroleum Fund if the government's plans to invest between 30 and 50 percent of the fund in foreign shares goes ahead. In 2001 the fund could spend between 400 and 600 milllion crowns on broker services.
- Aker Maritime has bought the state-owned shipyard Westamarine for 60 million crowns.
